title: Distributed In-Memory Key-Value Cache Engine in Rust with Consistent Hashing
problem: High-throughput distributed web applications exhaust relational database connection pools and disk I/O when handling read-heavy request spikes. Production caching systems mitigate this bottleneck, yet relying solely on prebuilt tools hides critical systems engineering concepts—lock-free concurrent memory management, cache replacement policies, thread contention mitigation, and network protocol framing. This project implements a high-throughput, distributed in-memory key-value cache engine from first principles in Rust. The system features a lock-free sharded storage map, segmented LRU and TinyLFU eviction, consistent hashing with virtual nodes for multi-node partitioning, an asynchronous Tokio TCP protocol parser, and request coalescing (singleflight) to prevent cache stampedes.
use_cases: Sub-millisecond session and authentication token caching for horizontally scaled APIs
Distributed database query result caching with automatic invalidation and stampede protection
High-frequency algorithmic trading feature store caching low-latency market state
hard_parts: Implementing lock-free sharded cache storage to eliminate mutex contention across high thread counts
Designing adaptive eviction combining frequency sketch (TinyLFU) and recency queues without lock contention
Distributing keys evenly across nodes using consistent hashing with virtual nodes and minimal key churn on node joins
Coalescing concurrent identical cache misses through singleflight synchronizers to eliminate database dogpiling
screener_signals: Idiomatic Rust implementation utilizing Tokio, parking_lot synchronization, and zero unsafe memory violations
Deterministic load test achieving over 100,000 requests/sec with p99 latency under 2 milliseconds on local hardware
Anti-fake verification script sending dynamic high-concurrency key bursts and asserting singleflight deduplication

components.name: Sharded Memory Cache Engine
components.purpose: Provides concurrent in-memory key-value storage partitioned across 32 stripes to minimize lock contention

components.name: TinyLFU Eviction Manager
components.purpose: Tracks key access frequencies with Count-Min sketches and evicts low-utility keys when memory limits trigger

components.name: Tokio Asynchronous TCP Server
components.purpose: Handles concurrent client TCP connections, parsing binary protocol frames and dispatching commands

components.name: Consistent Hashing Ring Router
components.purpose: Maps keys across cluster nodes using a 32-bit hash ring with 128 virtual nodes per physical instance

components.name: Singleflight Request Coalescer
components.purpose: Suppresses redundant upstream fetch operations by merging concurrent misses for identical keys

architecture.data_flow: Clients connect over TCP to the Tokio server; binary protocol frames are parsed into GET/SET commands; the Consistent Hashing Router determines target node ownership; the target node checks its Sharded Memory Cache; on hit, value bytes return immediately and TinyLFU frequency sketches update; on miss, the Singleflight Coalescer ensures only one upstream fetch executes while other concurrent requests await the shared result; returned data writes to memory and evicts candidates if memory limits are exceeded.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Strict memory quota bounds triggering TinyLFU eviction; read-write lock sharding preventing thread starvation.

worksheet.q5: Hard parts: lock-free sharded cache storage, adaptive TinyLFU eviction without lock contention, consistent hashing virtual node distribution, and singleflight stampede coalescing.
